payload.walk:
Q1 CLOSE ATOMICITY walked through the matrices - a close fails at any step and trunk must be left exactly as it was. VERDICT: ADDRESSED, carried by se.adr-tag-before-merge and the E3 black box. The walk: emptiness is detected before anything is written (F2), the tag is created before the merge (F3), and the merge itself is not committed until the filter has been applied (F5/F6) - so the three failure points all sit before the single trunk-visible write. AT-RISK RESIDUE, named honestly: the window between `merge --no-commit` and the commit leaves trunk's INDEX and working tree modified. A crash there does not move HEAD, so the recorded history is untouched, but the working copy would be left mid-merge and a human would have to abort it. The scenario says trunk is unchanged, and HEAD is - the working copy is not. Recorded as residue rather than claimed as addressed.

The stakeholder tensions walked as informal scenarios, since they are where the qualities actually bite:
- Reader vs auditor (trunk clean, record complete). ADDRESSED by se.adr-close-merge-filter plus se.adr-tag-before-merge; probed at run-aa90b5a988e9.
- Agent vs reader (durability vs noise). ADDRESSED by se.adr-milestone-commits-on-branch - the branch absorbs the frequency, trunk sees one commit.
- Owner vs agent (a ship must be trustworthy unattended). ADDRESSED by R2's refusal in E3.
- Auditor vs git maintainer (a complete record only grows). UNADDRESSED BY DESIGN, and correctly so - the accepted cost is recorded as se.raid-audit-frequency-shifts-the-balance rather than engineered away.

UNADDRESSED, deliberately out of scope: reading the withheld record back (i5e). Until that lands, the record is reachable by git command but not by any SE surface - which is why R12 keeps the archive listable in the meantime.
payload.fitness_candidates:
Six scenarios are measurable and should become automated checks at M7 rather than review-class judgments.

- FC1 trunk carries no event files after a close: assert that the merge commit's tree has no evidence, machines or state path for that iteration. Mechanical, exact.
- FC2 the merge commit has exactly two parents: a one-line assertion that catches any accidental slide into squash or fast-forward.
- FC3 withheld evidence is readable through the tag: read a known evidence path out of iter/<id> and compare it to what was written. This is the check that keeps the split from degrading into deletion, so it is the most valuable of the six.
- FC4 an empty branch refuses: close a fixture iteration whose branch has no commits and assert trunk's HEAD is unchanged and a named refusal was returned.
- FC5 atomicity under induced failure: make tagging fail, then assert trunk's HEAD is byte-identical and no merge was left pending. This is the direct automation of Q1, including a check on the residue named above.
- FC6 a milestone bless leaves a commit on the branch and a clean tree: the automation of UC-B.

All six are cheap fixture-repo tests, which is what makes them fitness functions rather than aspirations. FC5 is the one that would have caught nothing today but protects the property that matters most under unattended operation.
